meta.title: Aunt Sue's Bus List
meta.textType: a bus list with times in words

paragraphs: I am Lily, and Aunt Sue is my mom's younger sister. She is a nurse in Chiang Mai. She has two days off from work. She calls us on Wednesday evening. "I come to see you on Saturday," she says. Mom writes the day on the calendar. After the conversation, we look at the bus list. Aunt Sue takes the bus to our town.

The list has four buses from Chiang Mai. The first bus leaves at ten past six and arrives at half past ten. The second bus leaves at twenty to eight and arrives at twelve o'clock. The later buses leave at half past nine and at two o'clock. The trip takes about four hours. The bus goes on the motorway for most of the way. Each bus has a number on the front. It is fast, and it is safe.

"Which bus does she take?" I ask. "The second bus is popular," says Mom. "Many people take it, so she needs a seat early." Aunt Sue does not want to get up early on Saturday. So she takes the second bus. It arrives at twelve o'clock. I want to show her my new drawing. Mom and I leave the house at a quarter to twelve.

On Saturday, we wait at the bus station for fifteen minutes. The bus is not late. At twelve o'clock, Aunt Sue gets off. She waves her hand, and I run to her. Is the trip hard for her? "No, it is not," she says, and she smiles. We go home together. She has a small gift for Pip too. Pip jumps up and says, "Woof!"
